summary: Ono-i-Lau Airport (ONU) is a small regional airstrip serving Ono-i-Lau, one of the most remote inhabited islands in Fiji's Lau archipelago. Located near the 180° meridian in the far south of the country, the airport provides a vital air link for the island's small population to the rest of Fiji. It primarily accommodates light aircraft and occasional scheduled services connecting the isolated community to larger hubs.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Ono-i-Lau Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by small regional carriers operating light aircraft on infrequent scheduled or charter flights, often connecting through other Lau Islands.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities at ONU?
A: As a small domestic airstrip, formal customs and immigration services are limited; international travelers typically clear formalities at Nadi or Suva before onward flights.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Ono-i-Lau?
A: The dry season from May to October generally offers the most reliable weather for flights, as tropical cyclones can disrupt service during the wet season.

Q: How long is the runway at Ono-i-Lau Airport?
A: The airport has a single short runway suitable only for small propeller aircraft due to its limited length and basic infrastructure.
transport_tips: Travelers typically reach Ono-i-Lau by first flying into Suva or another Lau Island stop, then transferring to a light aircraft operated by a regional carrier. Ground transport on the island is minimal, so arranging a local pickup in advance is highly recommended. The remote location means flights can be delayed or rescheduled due to weather, so building flexibility into travel plans is essential.
local_tip: Bring cash in small denominations and any specialty supplies you need, as the island has very limited shops and no ATMs—residents are accustomed to visitors planning well in advance.
